name: Wisconsin Medical Supplies
old_description: The COVID-19 pandemic swiftly and powerfully showed us how unprepared the United States was to provide for our healthcare professionals and citizens in the event of this unprecedented emergency.
about:
Wisconsin Medical Supplies operates from Tempe, Arizona, with additional shipping operations in Wisconsin. The company emerged in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, which exposed the United States' lack of preparedness to supply healthcare professionals and citizens with essential protective equipment. The founders were moved by reports of frontline nurses and physicians resorting to bandanas and hand-sewn scraps, and they set out to produce American-made personal protective equipment.

The company manufactures NIOSH-certified N95 filtering facepiece respirators, three-layer and four-layer surgical face masks, and face shields. All products are labeled as made in the USA and are produced in an FDA-registered facility. The product line spans consumer packs to bulk quantities, with pricing ranging from $15.99 for a two-pack of face shields to $2,800 for large N95 orders, indicating capacity for both small and high-volume needs.

Primary customers include healthcare providers, hospitals, and individual consumers seeking domestically produced PPE. The company serves the medical and healthcare industries, with an emphasis on supplying NIOSH-approved respiratory protection and FDA-listed surgical masks. No specific institutional clients are named in the available information.

Wisconsin Medical Supplies states that it was founded to address the nation's reliance on foreign sources for critical medical supplies. The company's messaging stresses self-reliance: "We need to be self-reliant for our country's vital medical supplies," and it highlights domestic manufacturing as a core differentiator.

about:
Witonics operates from Ames, Iowa, as an online retailer of electronic components and repair kits. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company stocks a wide range of fuses — glass, ceramic, automotive, thermal, pico, and microwave types — from brands such as Bussmann, Littelfuse, Ferraz Shawmut (Mersen), Daito, Fuji, and SIBA. It also offers capacitor replacement kits for television and monitor power or inverter boards, along with individual capacitors, ICs, semiconductors, resistors, transistors, and diodes. Witonics notes that it is not an authorized distributor for Bussmann, Littelfuse, or Mersen products.

The business serves customers needing automotive fuses and electronic repair parts, including hobbyists, repair technicians, and service shops that replace capacitors in consumer displays. The product catalog spans industrial fuse series and component-level kits for board-level repair.

Witonics emphasizes RoHS-compliant inventory and fast shipping, with customer reviews highlighting quick delivery and responsive service. The capacitor kits target common failure symptoms such as slow startup, flickering screens, clicking noises, and power-LED issues in TVs and monitors.

name: Woeber Mustard Company
old_description: WE’VE SPENT THE LAST 110 years FIGURING IT OUT. HERE ARE A FEW HIGHLIGHTS.
about:
Woeber Mustard Company has been operating in Springfield, Ohio since its founding in 1905. The family-owned business traces its roots to the Woeber family, with Ray Woeber becoming the face of the brand as the "Mustard Man" in 1945. Over more than a century, the company has remained under family stewardship, building a reputation for condiments produced in its Midwestern facility.

The company manufactures a range of condiments including mustard, horseradish, mayonnaise, vinegar, lemon juice, and various dips. In addition to its branded lines, Woeber offers private-label production for food service and retail partners. All products are made at the Springfield plant, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volumes.

Woeber serves two primary channels: food service operators and retail distributors. Its products reach restaurants, institutional kitchens, and grocery shelves across the United States. The private-label program allows customers to develop custom formulations under their own brands.

The company attributes its longevity to family pride and a hands-on passion for mustard and horseradish quality. The legacy of the Mustard Man symbolizes a culture of innovation and fun that continues to guide product development today.

name: Wolf River Electric
old_description: Wolf River Electric is a locally owned solar energy company providing high-quality residential and commercial solar panel installations, including solar power systems throughout Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, North Dakota, and South Dakota. Founded by a team of passionate individuals about clean energy, we specialize in custom solar solutions designed for long-term performance and maximum savings. Committed to sustainability, innovation, and local service, we’re helping homeowners and businesses reduce energy costs and embrace renewable power—one solar panel system at a time.
about:
Wolf River Electric is headquartered in Isanti, Minnesota. Founded by a group of friends passionate about clean energy, the locally owned company began as a grassroots effort to make solar power accessible across the Upper Midwest.

The firm provides turnkey solar energy solutions for homes and businesses, including photovoltaic panel installation, battery storage integration, electric-vehicle charging station setup, smart-home technology upgrades, general electrical wiring services, and solar-integrated roofing. Crews handle design, permitting, utility interconnection, and ongoing monitoring, operating across Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, North Dakota, South Dakota, Michigan, and Illinois.

Customers range from individual homeowners seeking net-zero electricity to commercial property owners reducing operating costs. The company cites projects for Xcel Energy customers and residential clients such as the Totusek household, and emphasizes a collaborative, “pack” culture that aims to keep projects on schedule and within budget.

Wolf River Electric differentiates itself with a 25-year workmanship warranty and a full-service model that bundles solar, storage, EV, electrical, and roofing under one contract. The founders frame the business as a community-driven movement toward energy independence rather than a traditional contractor relationship.

name: Wood Castle Company Store
old_description: Trusted by Oregon families since 1978 — real hardwood furniture crafted to last generations.
about:
Wood Castle Company Store, based in Albany, Oregon, has been crafting solid wood furniture since its founding in 1978. The family-owned business began with a focus on heirloom-quality pieces built to last generations, serving homeowners throughout the Willamette Valley.

The company manufactures bedroom, dining, occasional, storage, and limited-edition furniture collections using sustainably sourced domestic hardwoods. Its production combines time-tested woodworking techniques — including mortise-and-tenon and dovetail joinery — with precision machinery to achieve tight-fitting components and reinforced construction. The factory operates on hydroelectric power and reports that approximately 99 percent of wood fiber is used or recycled, minimizing waste.

Wood Castle sells directly to residential customers through its Albany showroom and offers local delivery to communities such as Corvallis, Salem, Newport, and Lincoln City. Its furniture is designed for everyday use, with heavy-duty drawer glides and reinforced drawer bottoms intended to ensure long-term reliability.

The business emphasizes longevity over trends, citing a commitment to domestic materials, renewable energy, and construction methods that prioritize repairability and durability. Custom options are available, allowing buyers to tailor pieces to specific spaces.

name: Wood Technologies, LLC
old_description: From retail to healthcare, airports to hospitality, we design, engineer, and build precision fixtures and interiors.
about:
Wood Technologies, LLC was founded on January 25, 2001, in Grabill, Indiana, by Benjamin as a custom architectural millwork and cabinetry company targeting commercial markets. In January 2015, ownership transferred to his wife, Lydiann Lengacher, who had been involved in operations; she now serves as Manager and Partnership Representative. The business is certified as a Woman-Owned Business Enterprise.

The company designs, engineers, and fabricates precision fixtures, casework, and millwork for commercial interiors. Its production facility in rural Indiana combines traditional craftsmanship with modern manufacturing, including CNC machining, laminating, edge banding, finishing, and integration of materials such as acrylic, aluminum, Corian, glass, laminate, marble, melamine, metal, mirror, plastic, plywood, quartz, and steel. Services extend to 3D design, prototyping, high-volume manufacturing, project management, installation support, warehousing, and logistics, with shipments across all 50 states and into Canada.

Wood Technologies serves retail, hospitality, healthcare, corporate, and airport environments. Its client base includes general contractors, architects, designers, and corporate end users. Notable projects referenced include work for Tempur Pedic, Krewe Eyewear, Serena & Lily, and LaGuardia Airport.

The company emphasizes end-to-end expertise—design, engineering, fabrication, finishing, and logistics under one roof—to reduce handoffs and ensure consistent quality. Its woman-owned status is highlighted as a diversity asset for government and corporate projects, and it cites a proven track record of on-time, on-budget delivery for multi-location rollouts.

name: Wood and Water MN
old_description: Wood + Water is founded by Ashley Mellgren. Ashley grew up around the construction world and always loved making things by hand. Junior year in high school she made a bookcase for her parents in a wood working class, this is where her passion began. Throughout college, she didn’t have the place or money to start making decor and furniture like she aspired to, but she still made things when she would visit her parents at home. After graduating college and getting her own workshop, she desired to make anything and everything she could. If you think of it- she can make it!
about:
Wood and Water MN operates from Lauderdale, Minnesota, where founder Ashley Mellgren established the business after graduating college and acquiring her own workshop. Mellgren, who grew up around construction, traces her passion for making things by hand to a high school woodworking class where she built a bookcase for her parents.

The company produces custom wall art, furniture, and a variety of decorative odds and ends. Every piece is made from scratch and hand cut using various saws and hand tools; the shop does not use laser cutters. Offerings include pallet signs, seasonal signs, Minnesota-themed decor, lake signs, coffee tables, wine racks, headboards, bed frames, kitchen islands, barn doors, corn hole boards, and custom business logo signs.

Wood and Water serves both residential customers and commercial clients seeking custom signage and built-in furniture. The business emphasizes a collaborative approach, inviting customers to request any custom woodwork they can imagine.

Mellgren started the venture to fulfill a lifelong desire to make anything and everything she could, and the company differentiates itself by insisting on fully handcrafted, from-scratch production without laser cutting.

name: WoodLab
old_description: WoodLab is a homegrown woodshop based in Eagle, Idaho. Since 2017, we’ve handcrafted
about:
WoodLab operates from Eagle, Idaho, where it was founded in 2017 as a homegrown woodshop. The company began by crafting custom furniture from locally rescued urban wood, serving the Boise area and the broader Treasure Valley.

The shop handcrafts solid wood and epoxy river tables, custom art pieces, and ready-to-ship furniture. Its processes include live-edge slab selection, epoxy casting in colors such as multi-grey and dolphin grey, and concealed hardware installation that leaves no visible fasteners. An interactive online design tool lets customers specify wood species, epoxy color, leg style, and dimensions for a base price estimate. Finished pieces ship nationwide via LTL freight and internationally.

Customers range from residential buyers to commercial clients outfitting boardrooms and conference rooms. The product line includes dining tables, coffee tables, charcuterie boards, and wall art sculptures. WoodLab serves the Treasure Valley locally while fulfilling orders across the United States and overseas.

The company emphasizes its use of locally rescued urban wood and a hidden-hardware approach as key differentiators. The custom design tool streamlines collaboration, allowing clients to visualize projects before production begins.

about:
Wooden Specialties was founded in 1988 in Lafayette, Louisiana, by cabinetmaker Bryan Fontenot. Operating in the Acadiana region, the company began as a one-man shop focused on handcrafted cabinetry and has grown into a full-service custom cabinet builder serving homeowners across the area.

The company designs, manufactures, and installs custom cabinets for kitchens, bathrooms, living rooms, and closets. All work is performed in-house, from initial concept through final installation, with an emphasis on handcrafted construction and precision detail. While specific facility size and headcount are not disclosed, the firm reports hundreds of completed residential projects over more than three decades.

Wooden Specialties serves residential clients throughout Lafayette and the broader Acadiana region. Its customer base consists primarily of homeowners seeking custom cabinetry for new construction and remodeling projects; the company notes that a large share of new business comes from client referrals.

The founder’s original passion for cabinetmaking remains the stated differentiator: an uncompromising commitment to handcrafted quality and precision detail, coupled with a dedication to guiding customers through the entire design-build-install process.
